report:
Fresh review of the current associated_identity claim, all four ordinary implementation entries, and both ordinary associated tests. No TODO or N/A entries exist. The requirements are separate stable function/type/constant symbols for both trait and impl owners, ownership attachment, repeatable retrieval, and preservation of identity and owner when siblings move.

associated.rs supplies LocalAssociatedItemKey(kind, name, occurrence). Both lower_items and membership enumeration compute the same keys and invoke the per-owner tracked local_trait_associated_item/local_impl_associated_item queries. keyed_source_item matches kind/name and occurrence rather than a global sibling position. Consequently adding another named sibling and moving a named item among siblings retain the minting query key. Each of lower_item's three branches creates the corresponding concrete symbol and passes Some(owner). The three other associated implementation files define LocalFnSym, LocalConstSym, and LocalTypeAliasSym with name, scope, and owner as identity fields; CST and span are tracked mutable detail. The complete files, beyond the association previews, were inspected. No relevant behavior is missing from those associations.

The complete trait_items_have_stable_symbols_and_owner_identity test destructures method, associated function, type and constant symbols, explicitly checks method/type/constant ownership, and compares membership enumeration against semantic enumeration for the complete collection. This gives a second retrieval path with actual symbol equality assertions. Its binder/signature assertions are additional evidence for other claims, not a replacement for identity assertions. The complete moving_associated_items_preserves_symbol_query_keys test covers all six combinations of trait/impl with function/type/constant. For each it adds a preceding sibling and separately tests reorder; both edits are reversed. Its helper checks ownership on the visited symbols and retrieves the target by name. The test asserts that a symbol-keyed observer never reruns after either forward or reverse changes. The captured ObservedSymbol helper interns the symbol itself and its tracked observer has no body/detail dependencies. The captured Database logging records WillExecute, drains between observations, and is installed by the default database constructor. Reminting the target would create a new observer key and fail the visible assertions. Fixture setup and persistent source-file handling were captured as dependencies.

Together these tests exercise repeated retrieval, all three concrete kinds and both owners, ownership checks and stable identity under insertion, removal by reversing insertion, and sibling reorder. Source inspection also confirms kind/name occurrence distinguishes same-named entries rather than collapsing them; the explicit movement scenarios use distinct named declarations. All current ordinary evidence is substantive and no deferral is being silently approved. No suspected behavioral violation was identified. No Rust edits were needed. This refresh is source inspection only: I ran review start/read/record commands, not behavior tests; current test execution is delegated centrally to root by the captured instructions, and earlier test results are not asserted as current execution evidence.
